quest.title: A Deceit Called Happiness
quest.description: The financial troubles at the Aisa Bathhouse appear to be almost over when a sudden turn of events turns everything on its head. You and Mizuki soon realize that the root cause of the crisis still persists...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x375, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mizuki, we're here to book our next therapy appointment...

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Agh... It hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... What's wrong with them?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: They've been like this ever since they woke up...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...It's an extreme case of indigestion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How come? Did they eat too many nightmares last night?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: I doubt it... We only had four customers yesterday, including you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon blames the other two...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You're right. Something's definitely wrong with their nightmares... Our ability to digest dreams isn't just a matter of quantity. It depends on the emotional intensity, too.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Point being, no normal person should ever have a nightmare of this magnitude...

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: *retching*

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: The situation is dire. If I can't find a way to help them digest the dreams soon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What can we do? Let us help!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: We need to find those two customers from yesterday, and figure out the cause of their bad dreams. Without knowing that, I have no way of treating them.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, I know you spoke to them both. Think you can track them down?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Hmm, they did say they were gonna get counselling from Emura Ichigensai again. Chances are, that's where we'll find them!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Lead the way. I'm coming with you.

talks.objective: Go to Emura Ichigensai's place of business

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Y'know, I went out to sea earlier today, but was so distracted that I lost my net... Ah well, it's not a big deal though.

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Yeah, I messed up today too... but hey, what's the big deal? A few bandits got away, it's not the end of the world, hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you two! Murasaki and Shion are sick, and it's all because of your bad dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Whoa, someone's in a bad mood, huh? So funny, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: I know, right? Hehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're acting so weird! Paimon was pretty aggressive just now, but they don't seem offended at all...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...Allow me. Gentlemen, do you still remember visiting Aisa Bathhouse last night for dream regulation therapy?

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Did we?

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: I don't think so...?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Huh... Do you recall having any bad dreams recently?

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: No, why would I? What in this world could be so bad that it'd give me nightmares?

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Hmm... Nope, nothing comes to mind. Bad dreams must be highly irregular, surely? You don't have to look far to see that life is beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is going on? It's like they've completely forgotten what they did last night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although, Paimon can believe what they're saying. They don't exactly seem troubled by nightmares... Does that mean Emura Ichigensai's counselling actually works?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #No, they're clearly not in their right minds... {NICKNAME}, Paimon, focus hard for a second. I'm gonna try something a little unorthodox...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, what did you do...?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Entered their subconscious minds. I noticed they've both become disassociated from their subconscious, meaning I can access it — similarly to how I enter people's dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: No, nooo! Those thugs, I won't let them get away with this! I won't!!!

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: The sea's too rough today... I should stay on dry land till things calm down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: As you can see, their troubles haven't gone anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Susukida seems to have a short fuse, which causes him to act out of line. I'm sure this has caused him a lot of grief in his line of work.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: As for Umihiko... I believe he developed a fear of stormy waves after a near-death experience. Now, he's reluctant to sail out to sea at all, which is having a devastating impact on his livelihood.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Their negative emotions have been isolated from their conscious minds and left to float around in their subconscious. That's why on the outside, the only emotion they appear to feel is happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: But those suppressed emotions will only continue to fester in their subconscious, eventually turning into the nightmares that have been giving Murasaki and Shion indigestion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did this happen?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...If it's Emura Ichigensai's doing, I guess he's not the straightforward conman we thought he was. Maybe he really does have ways of influencing human emotions. That would explain why no one has blown the whistle on him yet...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Did you notice anything strange when you came here yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not really. They were a lot more serious than today...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, since you ask...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You remember the strange dream from yesterday, and recount it to Mizuki.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure kept that one quiet!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't think much of it at the time.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh, no no no... Look, we have to find this Emura Ichigensai right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mizuki... What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #Something inhuman is at work in Emura Ichigensai. {NICKNAME}'s dream confirms that... He has victimized everyone who has received his so-called counselling.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: If we don't find and stop him as soon as possible, his victims may well suffer irreversible damage to their psyches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes... Well, guess we'd better press these guys a little harder. Do you know when Emura Ichigensai will be here next?

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: What's with the urgency? Why does it matter when he shows up?

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Yeah, he'll turn up when he's ready. No point trying to rush him, heh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is infuriating!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...You do remember what happened last night. Both of you.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Only, you don't want to talk about it, because you can't reconcile the presence of a nightmare with the happiness you presently feel.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Just thinking about it brings up an overwhelming sense of being torn apart. You can't quite put it into words, but you fear you're a hair's breadth away from a total breakdown... Is that about right?

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: ...Please, stop. Everything will be fine as long as we don't think about it...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Emura Ichigensai's treatment has clearly left you wounded and vulnerable. But don't worry — I'm not here to snap you out of your denial.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...At least, as long as you answer our question.

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Alright... But seriously, we really have no idea. We've asked already, and all we know is that he's not coming today.

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Yeah, uh... apparently yesterday's session kind of... tired him out.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Is he trying to hide from me again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They really don't know anything? Darn. Looks like we've hit a dead end...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: I don't suppose you know where he lives, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No. We did ask yesterday, but even his guard didn't know.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: In that case...

choices.text: Have you found out what you came here for?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Yes, I suppose... Now that I know what's causing their bad dreams, I can administer the correct treatment...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Honestly, you've already done your part by bringing me here. I can't keep troubling you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't forget we wanna book our next therapy session! The sooner you stop having to worry about Emura Ichigensai, the sooner we get you all to ourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, we're not gonna quit until all this is resolved, and the bathhouse is back to business as usual!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Looks like I have no choice but to accept your help again. I have to make sure Murasaki and Shion get the treatment they need.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Still, I'm gonna need your full cooperation. If you do find Emura Ichigensai, please do not approach him. Just send me a message and keep an eye on him until I arrive.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: The last thing I want is for you to put yourself in harm's way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, don't worry about that! You should see some of the other bad guys we've taken down in our time. This guy's small potatoes compared to them!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Alright, sure. We'll keep our distance and send a message, heh.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Very good. Let's get going then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Pretty bold claim, saying you'll track this guy down. It's nice of you to give Mizuki one less thing to worry about and all, but... what the heck do we do now? What if we can't find him?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Cause in case you hadn't noticed, these guys are hopeless. They don't know anything!

choices.text: Yep, they definitely have no idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're right — she was the one who tipped us off about this place yesterday! She probably knows way more than she let on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no time to lose! To the Grand Narukami Shrine!

choices.text: But I suspect Miko knows something...
Are you able to help Murasaki and Shion now?

talks.objective: Go to the Grand Narukami Shrine and look for Miko

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's usually somewhere around here...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Here for a fortune slip, little ones? Or visiting a friend?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where did you come from...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Lady Guuji.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: That was a little lukewarm. You're starting to sound a lot like her... But pleasantries aside, what's the matter? You look rather out of sorts.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You may remember I dropped a not-so-subtle hint as to his whereabouts yesterday. You mean to tell me you still haven't found him?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aha, so you did bring him up on purpose!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...Let's not lose focus here. You're here to ask for my help. So, would you mind explaining the situation to me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, fair enough... We went to the place you mentioned, but he slipped through our fingers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next thing we heard was, he's not seeing patients there anymore — apparently, he loves his peace and solitude... So obviously, we've got no idea where to find him now...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh* And after the lengths I went to to get you that location...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunno if this helps, but we did learn some other stuff about him yesterday. For example, a guy matching Emura Ichigensai's description came to Mizuki for therapy once — only his name was "Emura Chuuya."

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Wait, what? Emura Chuuya?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know him?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I once asked the Yae Publishing House to host an event for contributors to the readers' letters column. I had hoped it might be a fun chance to meet some like-minded people and chat... until he showed up.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Are you telling me that Emura the hell-raiser and Emura the healer are the same person?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Based on everything we've learned so far, it certainly looks that way.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright. Well, in that case... give this address a try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Really? Who chooses to live in a place like that?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: This was the delivery address he gave to the Yae Publishing House once, when he placed an order for several dozen books in one go. He also requested to pay on receipt.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The warehouse took one look and assumed it must be some kind of prank, so they rejected the order... Earning them an honorable mention in his complaint letter.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Of course, with the benefit of hindsight, it's rather obvious why he lives there. Someone as antisocial as him wouldn't be welcome anywhere else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've got a point... Well, we clearly made the right decision coming to talk to you!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm just glad I could help my old friend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean Mizuki? So, you really do want to help her?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I can tell that she's invested an awful lot into the Aisa Bathhouse. It's only natural for me to show some concern when I see a friend's business in trouble.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? 'Cause yesterday, it looked more like you were looking for a fight...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I assume Mizuki has told you that we're competitors?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: She has always believed that, ever since we were classmates. And now that I'm the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, I'm sure she must feel the need to prove herself through her endeavors at the Aisa Bathhouse.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The last thing she'd want is for me of all people to swoop in and save the day the moment the going gets tough... So if I want to help, I have to be mindful of her feelings and tread delicately.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's rare to see you being so considerate...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'll take that as a compliment. Mizuki's always so considerate towards others — it would be nice for someone to reciprocate once in a while.

choices.text: Well, since you're in a difficult position...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well done, you took the hint. Now, while I'm sure you'd love to chat longer, you seemed to be in a great hurry when you arrived. Shouldn't you be on your way?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! C'mon, let's send a message to Mizuki right away!

choices.text: ...Maybe I can do the honors instead?
Do you know where we can find Emura Ichigensai?

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: Ahh, what should I do about work...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is just my luck...

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll look after the bathhouse.
